claims.label: Host Says Tyler Robinson Uses "Car" Rather Than "Vehicle" in 2022 Police Bodycam Footage
claims.claim: The host says Tyler Robinson refers to it as his car, not his vehicle, in the 2022 police bodycam footage she plays, in which his mother is said to have to "shuttle over from where she's at to her car", which she contrasts with the vocabulary of the federal text messages.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the original 2022 bodycam video and full transcript; compare against the released federal text messages.

claims.label: Host Says Robinson Saying "Car" Rather Than "Vehicle" Is How Most English Speakers Talk
claims.claim: Host states (via commentary on A-1171.1) that Robinson's everyday use of "car" rather than "vehicle" is typical of ordinary American English speakers.
claims.investigative_direction: Independent corpus sampling of Robinson's other recorded speech; comparison with general American English usage.

claims.label: Brooksby Says a Retired Friend Called at 8:02 p.m. Saying He Knew Who the Shooter Was
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, Nate Brooksby says that at 8:02 p.m. a friend who has been retired a few years, whom the host describes as a former detective, called to say he knew who the Charlie Kirk shooter was.
claims.investigative_direction: Cross-reference call logs and the court filings already referenced by Brooksby (court documents where the friend was named as a "retired Washington County deputy").

claims.label: Brooksby Says He Withheld the Retired Deputy's Identity to Protect Him
claims.claim: Brooksby stated that he did not initially disclose the friend as a former detective and only referenced him generally as "retired law enforcement"; he argued that the court documents were what ultimately revealed the title.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull the cited court documents and compare Brooksby's public statements with the actual filed text.

claims.label: Brooksby stated Tyler Robinson had suicidal ideations during the initial phone call
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, Nate Brooksby says that during the initial call "some information was provided" about Tyler "potentially having some suicidal ideations" and a remote area of Washington County, and that the parents convinced him not to do that.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the full unedited press-conference audio and any internal law-enforcement notes from the call.

claims.label: Brooksby stated Tyler Robinson came in willingly out of fear of being shot by law enforcement
claims.claim: In a clip the host plays, Brooksby says Tyler's arrival at his office was treated "as delicate and as soft as possible" because he was "fearful of a SWAT team hit" on his house or of being shot by law enforcement.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain any negotiated-surrender documentation; reconcile with the contemporaneous suicide-ideation claim.

claims.label: Lance's Instagram posts establish a romantic relationship with Tyler Robinson
claims.claim: Host presents Lance's Halloween-era Instagram caption ("I forgot to post my boyfriend is the best. Love you.") and a photo of Tyler with a mustache as evidence that Tyler and Lance were in a romantic relationship.
claims.investigative_direction: Recover archived versions of Lance's Instagram handle (host notes it has since been removed); cross-reference with any retained screenshots in the investigative file.

claims.label: Mike Mitchell retired from the Washington County Sheriff's Office after 24+ years
claims.claim: Per the retirement-celebration post the host shows, Detective Mike Mitchell served Washington County for "over 24 years … starting in the jail back in 1999."
claims.investigative_direction: Verify against Washington County personnel records and any prior news coverage of Mitchell's career.

claims.label: The retirement-celebration post is the only public trace of Mike Mitchell
claims.claim: The host says that despite a career of 25 years in the police force she could not find a single trace of Mike Mitchell in old newspapers, and presents the retirement post as the only trace of him she could find.
claims.investigative_direction: Conduct independent newspaper archive search (local Utah papers, Provo, St. George) and Washington County internal award/honor records.

claims.label: Host Says Brooksby's Suicidal-Ideation Account Confusingly Conflicts With Her Source
claims.claim: The host says it is confusing that Nate Brooksby tells us Tyler is suicidal, when her source says Tyler is not suicidal and went to the police station so as not to risk being shot.
claims.investigative_direction: Seek clarification from Brooksby or from the Washington County Sheriff's Office on which account is operative.

claims.label: Phil Lyman Says He Parked in the TMZ Footage Driveway About 10 Minutes Before the Shooter Walked By
claims.claim: In his Kayleigh McEnany interview, Phil Lyman says the driveway is his aunt's and that he parked his gray CRV there probably 10 minutes before the shooter walked by; McEnany puts his 11:30 a.m. parking and the 11:49 a.m. footage at 19 minutes apart, and the host restates the 19 minutes.
claims.investigative_direction: Timestamp the TMZ footage independently and reconcile with Lyman's stated parking time.

claims.label: Host Says Lyman's Family Owns Twelve Homes in the Area
claims.claim: In the Kayleigh McEnany interview, Phil Lyman describes the area as his childhood neighborhood and his relatives' neighborhood; the host says his family owns twelve homes right there.
claims.investigative_direction: Pull county property records for the relevant street and verify ownership chain.

claims.label: Phil Lyman publicly described "two goth girls" as unfrightened near the shooting scene on Alex Jones
claims.claim: In an Alex Jones interview, Phil Lyman recounted being at the east end of the venue, hearing a loud bang, seeing people ducking behind concrete retaining walls, and encountering two "very goth, very black" girls who were not running; he reported that one girl said "Go f yourselves" while looking down at fleeing people.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the unedited Alex Jones segment and any witness statements regarding the two individuals described.

claims.label: Phil Lyman stated on local Utah news that he was backstage with Charlie Kirk before the shooting
claims.claim: In a local Utah news interview the host plays, Phil Lyman stated he was backstage, throwing hats, and standing next to the stage before going to "meet some of my friends" away from the stage.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain the unedited local Utah news segment; compare timeline with the Alex Jones account.

claims.label: Phil Lyman posted an Instagram video on September 10, 2025 at ~11:30 PM describing proximity and a "200 yard kill shot"
claims.claim: In his own Instagram video, Phil Lyman stated he was heading back from Salt Lake to Blanding on the night of the shooting, wanted to swing by UVU campus to thank officers, and recounted being "very close this morning" to where Charlie Kirk was, meeting Charlie backstage, deciding to "go up top," and concluding it was a "200 yard kill shot" from the roof.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm upload timestamp and metadata on Instagram; obtain the original unedited video if still available.

claims.label: Shane Lyman publicly retraced the shooter's steps near his grandmother's house
claims.claim: Shane Lyman [Shaner Broderick]'s Instagram post presented a map of the area near his grandmother's house and stated he and friends retraced the shooter's steps, taking "pictures in the exact place that the security cameras caught him"; the image showed Converse-brand footprints.
claims.investigative_direction: Recover archived version of Shane Lyman's Instagram post; verify the grandmother's house address against the property records already referenced by Phil Lyman.

claims.label: Shane Lyman's Instagram included side-by-side staircase photos with three unidentified individuals
claims.claim: Shane Lyman [Shaner Broderick]'s Instagram post showed side-by-side photos of Shane and three friends on a staircase; the host states she could not find two of the individuals on his friends list.
claims.investigative_direction: Identify the two friends via cross-reference with Shane's social graph or via direct outreach.

claims.label: Phil Lyman Asked for Nick's Address, Came to His Home and Asked About the Host's Investigation
claims.claim: Per Nick's account to host, Phil Lyman messaged Nick for his address (something he had not previously had), arrived at Nick's home, looked out the window nervously, sat at the table, and asked questions about the host's investigation.
claims.investigative_direction: Obtain any corroborating records (Ring/doorbell footage, phone logs, text screenshots) and a contemporaneous written statement from Nick.

claims.label: Nick Says Phil Lyman Offered Independent Investigator Ian Carroll a Tour of the Area
claims.claim: Per Nick's account as relayed by the host, Phil Lyman offered a tour of the area to Ian Carroll, who was conducting a separate on-the-ground investigation; Nick found this "weird" given that Lyman lives four hours away.
claims.investigative_direction: Confirm via Ian Carroll's own public statements and any travel/timeline records.

claims.label: Nick supplied the black-suit food-court photo to host
claims.claim: Host states that Nick sent the food-court photo of a person in a black suit and dark sunglasses with a strap hanging from a bag into the tips box early in the investigation.
claims.investigative_direction: Recover the original image and metadata; identify the individual depicted.

claims.label: Host acknowledges Marzy's keyholing-fragmentation bullet theory as new information
claims.claim: Host states she was previously unaware of "keyholing" and acknowledges Marzy's comment about intentionally keyholed rounds for tumbling/fragmentation damage as new to her.
claims.investigative_direction: Independent forensic review of recovered bullet(s) for keyholing signatures.

claims.label: Host concurs with Caitlyn Derrian's characterization of her journalism
claims.claim: Host reads Caitlyn Derrian's supportive comment calling her a true model of real journalism and responds, "Yeah. I mean, my insatiable thirst is to figure out what happened that day."
claims.investigative_direction: N/A – rhetorical/statement of self-positioning, recorded for traceability only.

claims.label: Host concurs with multiple commenters that the people closest to Charlie are not investigating
claims.claim: Host agrees with Kristen Theoret's and Cassie's comments that the people closest to Charlie Kirk are moving on and not asking questions about the shooting, and also reads Kaya's comment ("It's 1963 all over again. They don't like people asking questions.").
claims.investigative_direction: Inventory public statements/actions (or silence) by named individuals close to Charlie Kirk.

claims.label: Host Agrees With Viewer Comments on a Staged World and Prayer for Investigators
claims.claim: Host concurs with Bitsy's comment about a "stage" narrative; responding to Miranda Allen's comment offering prayers, she says she really believes praying protection over the people trying to discover what happened is significant.
claims.investigative_direction: N/A – rhetorical/statement of self-positioning.

claims.label: Host Says Tyler Robinson Is Not Suicidal According to Her Source
claims.claim: The host says she wanted to get out quickly the information that Tyler Robinson is not suicidal, and that she knows this from her source.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare Washington County Sheriff's Office and court records of the surrender call (the 'suicidal ideations' remark) against the host's source. Ask whether the source can document the family's account.
claims.transcript_snippet: I genuinely   wanted to get the information out as soon as  possible that Tyler Robinson is not suicidal.   And I'm going to tell you how I know that.

claims.label: Host Says a Vetted Source Contacted Her Last Week With Answers to Lingering Questions
claims.claim: The host says that last week she was contacted by a source she vetted, whose information answered some of the lingering questions about the investigation (how the surrender worked, the federal text messages, the Dairy Queen photo).
claims.investigative_direction: The source is unnamed and nothing was shown. Ask the host to describe how the source was vetted, or have the source go on record or provide documents.
claims.transcript_snippet: Last week, I have to tell  you, I was contacted by a source who I vetted with   information that answered a lot of the lingering  questions that we've had about the investigation.

claims.label: Host Alleges Feds Withheld Dairy Queen Information and Are Watching the Dairy Queen
claims.claim: The host asks why the feds withheld information about the Dairy Queen and why they are allegedly stalking the Dairy Queen to see who comes in and out. She presents the source's account as one that could answer both questions.
claims.investigative_direction: Ask the host to say what the 'withheld' information is. Ask the Dairy Queen's staff or owners whether law enforcement has been watching the store. FBI and Utah County records of the Dairy Queen photo handling would also help.
claims.transcript_snippet: And why exactly did the   feds withhold that information at Dairy Queen? And  why are they allegedly stalking the Dairy Queen to   see who comes in and out?

claims.label: Host Says Robinson Has Never Confessed and Is Still Pleading Innocence
claims.claim: The host says Tyler Robinson has never confessed, that 'they' acknowledge he has never confessed, and that he is still pleading innocence on the shooting.
claims.investigative_direction: Check the charging documents and court filings for any confession or admission. Check Robinson's plea status and any statements by his defense counsel.
claims.transcript_snippet: First and foremost,  Tyler Robinson has never confessed. They   acknowledge that he has never confessed to this  crime and he still uh is pleading innocence on the   shooting.

claims.label: Source Says Robinson Was Bewildered by the Idea He Carved the Casings and Does Not Dispute the Gun Is His
claims.claim: The host says she was told Tyler Robinson was 'bewildered' by the idea that he carved the casings, and that he does not dispute the gun is his.
claims.investigative_direction: Compare with the casing engraving evidence in the charging documents and with Robinson's defense filings. Ask the host's source for corroboration.
claims.transcript_snippet: In fact, I was told that he was quote  unquote bewildered by the idea that he carved   casings. I should be clear, he does not dispute  the fact that it is his gun at all.

claims.label: Source Says Robinson Is Not a Gun Enthusiast and Does Not Hunt Like His Brothers
claims.claim: The host says that, according to her source, Tyler Robinson is not a gun enthusiast, does not hunt like his brothers do, and is apparently a fisherman.
claims.investigative_direction: Check hunting and fishing licence records, firearm purchase records and Robinson's social media posts. Ask the Robinson family's counsel.
claims.transcript_snippet: but Tyler is not exactly a gun enthusiast. He  doesn't hunt like his other brothers do. In fact,   he's apparently a fisherman.

claims.label: Source Says the Rifle Is a Custom-Made Family Heirloom Inherited by the Firstborn Son
claims.claim: The host says that, according to her source, Tyler Robinson has the gun because it is a custom-made family heirloom and he inherited it as the firstborn son.
claims.investigative_direction: Look for the rifle's make, serial number and ownership history in the ATF trace and the charging documents. Check public statements by the Robinson family or their counsel about how the gun came to Tyler.
claims.transcript_snippet: The reason that he  has that gun in the first place is because it is   in fact a custommade family heirloom. Tyler is  the firstborn son. So he inherited.

claims.label: Source Says the Robinson Family Are Fans of Charlie Kirk and Trump
claims.claim: The host says she is told the Robinson family are fans of Charlie Kirk and of Donald Trump, and that her source said Tyler, like many other conservatives, wished Trump would sometimes tone down his speech and rhetoric.
claims.investigative_direction: Check Robinson family voter registration, donations and public statements. The source is unnamed, so independent corroboration is needed.
claims.transcript_snippet: I am told  that they are fans of Charlie Kirk and they are   fans of Donald Trump. Although this source noted  that Tyler, like many other conservatives have   um expressed,

claims.label: Source Says Robinson Did Not Author the Federal Text Messages
claims.claim: The host says she is told that Tyler Robinson absolutely did not author the text messages, has no idea where they came from, and believes they are entirely fictionalized.
claims.investigative_direction: Request the forensic extraction reports for the messages and the device they came from. Check for any defense motion challenging the messages' authenticity.
claims.transcript_snippet: I am told that Tyler absolutely  did not author those text messages. What text   messages? He has no idea where these messages  came from. Uh believes that they are therefore   entirely fictionalized.

claims.label: Host Says Robinson Does Not Use the Word Vehicle According to the Source
claims.claim: The host says it turns out, per her source, that Tyler Robinson does not actually use words like 'vehicle'.
claims.investigative_direction: Review a larger sample of Robinson's recorded and written speech for use of 'vehicle'. The 2022 bodycam clip aired later in the episode (A-1171.1) is one data point.
claims.transcript_snippet: It turns out, you're  going to be shocked that he doesn't actually   use words like vehicle.

claims.label: Source Says Robinson's Parents Do Not Believe Their Son Committed the Crime
claims.claim: The host says she has learned that Tyler Robinson's father, and his parents, do not believe their son committed the crime. She says this is a far cry from what the media has told us.
claims.investigative_direction: Look for public statements by the Robinson parents or their counsel on their view of Tyler's guilt. Compare with the media accounts, including statements by Governor Cox.
claims.transcript_snippet: of most interest to me. what I've learned is that   his father uh does not believe his parents don't  believe that their son committed this crime.

claims.claim: The host recounts the media narrative that Tyler Robinson's father realized his son was guilty and phoned a friend to help convince him to turn himself in.
